title: PHY 101 ( UNINIGER ) : QUANTITIES, UNITS AND MEASUREMENTS
subject: PHY 101

questions.question: Which of the following describes a quantity?
questions.explanation: Quantity is any property of a body that can be measured.

questions.question: A quantity is measured using which of the following?
questions.explanation: A unit is the yardstick with which a quantity is measured.

questions.question: Fundamental quantities cannot be defined in terms of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Fundamental quantities are basic quantities that are independent of others.

questions.question: The measurement of volume in local markets uses which of the following?
questions.explanation: Rice and other grains are measured using cups, baskets, and bags in local settings.

questions.question: Fundamental quantities are independent of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Fundamental quantities are basic quantities that are independent of others.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental quantity?
questions.explanation: Temperature is one of the fundamental quantities that cannot be derived from others.

questions.question: Fundamental units are units of which quantities?
questions.explanation: Fundamental units are the units of fundamental quantities.

questions.question: The unit of mass is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The fundamental unit of mass is the kilogram.

questions.question: The unit of time is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The fundamental unit of time is the second.

questions.question: The unit of electric current is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The fundamental unit of electric current is the ampere.

questions.question: The unit of temperature is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The fundamental unit of temperature is the Kelvin.

questions.question: The unit of amount of substance is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The fundamental unit of amount of substance is the mole.

questions.question: The unit of luminous intensity is which of the following?
questions.explanation: The fundamental unit of luminous intensity is the candela.

questions.question: S.I. units are accepted by whom?
questions.explanation: S.I. units are internationally accepted standards of measurement.

questions.question: Derived quantities are obtained from which type of combination?
questions.explanation: Derived quantities are obtained from a simple combination of fundamental quantities.

questions.question: Which of the following is a derived quantity?
questions.explanation: Area is a derived quantity obtained from the combination of length and breadth.

questions.question: Derived units are obtained from which type of units?
questions.explanation: Derived units are obtained from a simple combination of fundamental units.

questions.question: The derived unit of velocity is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Velocity is displacement divided by time, giving the unit ms⁻¹.

questions.question: The derived unit of acceleration is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is change in velocity divided by time, giving the unit ms⁻².

questions.question: The derived unit of momentum is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Momentum is mass multiplied by velocity, giving the unit kg m s⁻¹.

questions.question: The derived unit of work or energy is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Work is force multiplied by distance, giving the unit kg m² s⁻².

questions.question: The derived unit of power is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Power is work done divided by time, giving the unit kg m² s⁻³.

questions.question: The derived unit of pressure is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area, giving the unit kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

questions.question: The derived unit of density is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume, giving the unit kg m⁻³.

questions.question: Derivation of units involves how many steps?
questions.explanation: There are six steps involved in deriving the unit of a physical quantity.

questions.question: The derivation of the unit of force leads to which expression?
questions.explanation: Force is mass multiplied by acceleration, giving the unit kg m s⁻².

questions.question: The derived unit of pressure can be expressed as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Pressure is force divided by area, which simplifies to kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

questions.question: Dimensions show how a quantity is made up in terms of which quantities?
questions.explanation: Dimensions show how a physical quantity is made up in terms of basic quantities.

questions.question: The three fundamental dimensions are length, mass, and what else?
questions.explanation: The three fundamental dimensions used in mechanics are length, mass, and time.

questions.question: The dimension of power is represented as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Power is work done divided by time, which gives the dimension ML²T⁻³.
